title: N-th magical number
statement: A positive integer is magical if it is divisible by a or b. Return the n-th magical number mod 10⁹+7 (n ≤ 10⁹; a, b ≤ 4 × 10⁴).
hints: How many magical numbers are ≤ x? x/a + x/b − x/lcm(a, b) (inclusion–exclusion).
That count is monotone in x: binary search for the smallest x with count ≥ n.

solution.explanation: Three tools at once: inclusion–exclusion counts multiples of a or b; lcm = a·b / gcd (Euclid's algorithm); and binary search on the answer because the count is monotone. A merge-like walk would take n = 10⁹ steps. Take the modulus only at the end: the binary search needs the true value.
